title: Grateful Dead Live at Public Hall on 1973-12-06
lineage: CD -> Adobe Audition v1.5 -> Samplitude Professional v10.22 -> FLAC
source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Cassette -> Dat -> CD

ai_review.summary: An excellent Miller soundboard capture of the legendary 12/6/73 Cleveland show, featuring a soaring, space‑filled Dark Star and an incendiary Here Comes Sunshine.
ai_review.review: The recording is widely praised as a pristine soundboard source that renders every instrument with clarity, letting Keith’s electric piano and Phil’s thunderous bass shine. Musically the night shines brightest on the mammoth Dark Star (which segues into Eyes > Stella Blue) and the fiery Here Comes Sunshine, delivering high‑energy improvisation throughout the set.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 20 reviews overwhelmingly praise both the performance (especially Dark Star and Here Comes Sunshine) and the Miller soundboard quality; only a handful of low‑star outliers mention personal taste, yielding an overall strong positive rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clear mix with superb instrument separation; reviewers note it as the best source available, no audience patches, and a faithful capture of the band’s interplay.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: A solid first set followed by a second set that builds from a space‑y, slow‑burn Dark Star into an energetic Eyes > Stella Blue sequence; overall pacing is praised for its balance of exploratory jams and tight rockers.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly lauded for his vibrant, inventive soloing and tone, especially during Dark Star and Here Comes Sunshine.
band_member_comments.Phil: Described as delivering “bass bombs,” leading the band with powerful, melodic lines; many call this one of his best performances.
band_member_comments.Bob: Noted for a nice tone and solid rhythm work, though fewer specific comments appear.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s electric piano receives high praise for its jazzy, shimmering presence that drives the Dark Star jam.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann (and occasional mention of Mickey) are highlighted as “on fire,” providing a steady yet dynamic foundation.
